title: Best drag-and-drop BI tools with AI assistants (2026): Tableau, Power BI, Zoho Analytics, and 6 more compared
summary: Tableau, Power BI, Zoho Analytics, Metabase and Qlik pair drag-and-drop builders with AI that builds charts. What each AI does, which plan unlocks it, and cost.
body_markdown:
The best drag-and-drop BI tools with AI assistants in 2026 are Tableau and Power BI for teams that want the deepest visual builders, Zoho Analytics and Metabase for small teams that want a cheap or free start, and Qlik Cloud Analytics and Domo for teams that would rather pay for capacity than per seat. The catch is that the AI often costs more than the builder: Power BI’s Copilot needs Fabric F2 or Premium P1 capacity, Tableau Agent needs Tableau Cloud+ or the Tableau+ bundle, and Zoho’s Ask Zia agent needs the Premium plan. Data Studio, Sigma, and Basedash round out the list, and every price below was checked on the vendor’s official page on October 22, 2026.


## What buyers ask when they compare drag-and-drop BI tools


These are the qualified questions that shaped the criteria, the table, and the FAQ:


- Which BI tool has the best drag-and-drop interface?
- What is the top drag-and-drop dashboard software with AI insights?
- Which analytics platforms combine drag-and-drop editors with LLM assistants that explain metric trends in plain English, with BigQuery integration?
- Which BI tools offer browser-based drag-and-drop exploration with usage-based pricing?
- What are the best AI-driven BI platforms for self-service dashboards?
- Can AI automatically create charts when I ask a question?
- How do I choose between a code-first BI tool and a drag-and-drop tool for mixed spreadsheet and SQL users?
- What is the best no-code dashboard builder for business data?


## How we evaluated drag-and-drop BI tools


1. **The builder.** What do you drag (fields onto shelves, steps in a query builder, spreadsheet columns), and can someone who doesn’t write SQL finish a chart alone?
2. **What the AI can build.** Does it create charts, report pages, or whole dashboards inside the builder, or only answer questions in a side panel?
3. **Which plan unlocks the AI.** Is it in the plan you would buy anyway, or does it need a higher edition, capacity, or credits?
4. **Pricing model and entry price.** Per seat, per capacity, or usage-based, as of October 2026.
5. **Warehouse connectivity and query model.** Native BigQuery, Snowflake, and Postgres connections, and whether charts query live or use extracts and imports.
6. **Governance.** Row-level security, SAML SSO, and SCIM, and the plan each needs.

## Tableau


**Best for:** analysts who build polished visual dashboards daily and want AI inside the same canvas.


Tableau is still the reference drag-and-drop builder: you drag fields onto the Rows, Columns, and Marks shelves, or pick a chart from Show Me, which suggests chart types for the fields you selected ([building views](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/buildmanual_shelves.htm) ). Tableau Agent “creates visualizations based on your data, just like Show Me,” and is in beta for dashboards ([Tableau Agent](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein.htm) ). On Tableau Cloud it needs Cloud+ or the Tableau+ bundle and a Creator or Explorer role. Tableau Pulse metric digests with AI insight summaries are included in Cloud Standard ([AI settings](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/setup_tabAI_site_setting.htm) ).


**Fact card: Tableau**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** per seat, annual only. Standard Creator $75, Explorer $42, Viewer $15 per user per month; Enterprise $115, $70, $35 ([Salesforce Tableau pricing](https://www.salesforce.com/analytics/tableau/?bc=HA) ;[tableau.com](https://www.tableau.com/pricing) lists Standard from $15). Cloud+ and Tableau+ are contact sales.
- **Free tier or trial:** Tableau Desktop Free Edition for local use; a Tableau Cloud trial that includes Tableau Agent; Desktop activates for 14 days.
- **Deployment:** Tableau Cloud, or Tableau Server on-premises or in your cloud.
- **Databases and query model:** Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL; live connections or extracts with full or incremental refresh ([extracts](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/extracting_data.htm) ).
- **Access control:** user filters, data policies (Data Management license), or database RLS ([RLS options](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/rls_options_overview.htm) ); SAML; SCIM, which requires SAML or OIDC ([SCIM](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/scim_config_online.htm) ).
- **AI features:** Tableau Agent for visualizations, Pulse insight summaries, Tableau Agent in Pulse on Tableau+.
- **Embedding:** Embedding API v3 with JWT-based RLS; usage-based embedded license.
- **Not ideal for:** small teams that want AI on a self-serve plan; the AI editions are sales-led.


## Power BI


**Best for:** Microsoft 365 organizations that already pay for Fabric or Premium capacity.


You select fields in the Data pane or drag them into a visual’s wells, such as the X-axis or Legend ([adding visuals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-report-add-visualizations-i) ). Copilot can “create and edit report pages by using natural language prompts” ([Copilot report creation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-create-report-service) ), so it drafts a drag-and-drop page you then adjust by hand. Read the licensing closely: Copilot needs paid Fabric capacity (F2 or higher) or Premium (P1 or higher), and “a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User (PPU) license alone isn’t sufficient” ([Copilot requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-introduction) ). The older Q&A visual retires in February 2027 ([Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/natural-language/q-and-a-intro) ).


**Fact card: Power BI**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Free; Pro $14 and Premium Per User $24 per user per month, paid yearly ([pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ); Copilot needs F2+ or P1+ capacity on top.
- **Free tier or trial:** free account; 60-day Fabric trial, though trial capacities don’t run Copilot.
- **Deployment:** cloud; Power BI Report Server on-premises, without Copilot.
- **Databases and query model:** Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL with Import (8 refreshes a day on Pro, 48 on PPU) or DirectQuery ([Snowflake connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/snowflake) ).
- **Access control:** DAX-based RLS roles that don’t apply to workspace Admins, Members, or Contributors ([RLS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/enterprise/service-admin-rls) ); Microsoft Entra ID sign-in and provisioning.
- **AI features:** the Copilot report pane (generally available) and a standalone Power BI agent (preview).
- **Embedding:** secure embed by iframe for licensed users; Power BI Embedded on capacity for customer-facing apps. Publish to web doesn’t support RLS.
- **Not ideal for:** Pro-only teams expecting Copilot, or Mac-first teams, since Power BI Desktop requires Windows ([requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/fundamentals/desktop-get-the-desktop) ).


## Data Studio


**Best for:** Google Cloud teams on BigQuery that want a free report builder with free chat on top.


Google renamed Looker Studio back to Data Studio in April 2026 ([Data Studio docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/welcome) ). You drag a field to a slot in a chart’s setup panel or straight onto the chart ([configure components](https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/studio/configure-report-components) ). Conversational Analytics became generally available on July 30, 2026, free for all users, but it answers from BigQuery data agents that you create in BigQuery ([Conversational Analytics](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/conversational-analytics-overview) ). Gemini in Data Studio, which writes calculated fields from plain English, needs Data Studio Pro and is in preview ([Gemini](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/gemini-overview) ). Generating charts on the report canvas from a prompt is not documented.


**Fact card: Data Studio**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** free for creators and viewers; Data Studio Pro $9 per user per project per month ([product page](https://cloud.google.com/data-studio) ).
- **Free tier or trial:** free tier; 30-day Pro trial.
- **Deployment:** cloud only.
- **Databases and query model:** native BigQuery and PostgreSQL (150,000 rows per Postgres query); Snowflake only through partner connectors. Live queries with a cache of 1 minute to 12 hours, 12 hours by default ([data freshness](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/manage-data-freshness) ).
- **Access control:** filter by email for row-level restrictions ([filter by email](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/filter-by-email-address) ); SSO and provisioning come from Google Workspace or Cloud Identity.
- **AI features:** Conversational Analytics on BigQuery data agents; Gemini calculated fields on Pro.
- **Embedding:** iframe only, always with a Data Studio watermark.
- **Not ideal for:** Snowflake shops, or governed per-user access outside Google identity.


## Metabase


**Best for:** small teams that want a free or low-cost builder non-SQL users learn quickly, with AI on their own API key.


The query builder is a graphical, step-by-step editor (pick data, join, filter, summarize, visualize) that produces charts anyone can drill into ([query builder](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/questions/query-builder/editor) ). Dashboards are a grid of cards you drag and resize. Metabot creates charts “using the query builder from a natural language query,” generates SQL, and explains charts, including from Slack ([Metabot](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/ai/metabot) ). Because the output is a query-builder question, not raw SQL, a non-technical user can open it and change a filter by hand. Your own Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, or Azure key works on every plan, open source included ([AI settings](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/ai/settings) ).


**Fact card: Metabase**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** open source free; Starter $100/mo for 5 users plus $6 per extra user (cloud only); Pro $575/mo for 10 users plus $12 per extra user; Enterprise from $20,000 a year ([pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing.md) ). Managed Metabase AI: first 1M tokens free, then $3.75 per 1M.
- **Free tier or trial:** free self-hosted open source; 14-day cloud trial.
- **Deployment:** cloud or self-hosted.
- **Databases and query model:** BigQuery, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and more; live queries.
- **Access control:** row and column security on Pro and Enterprise, bypassed by groups with native SQL access ([permissions](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/permissions/row-and-column-security) ); SAML and SCIM on Pro and Enterprise.
- **AI features:** Metabot for charts, SQL, and explanations; an MCP server on all plans.
- **Embedding:** guest embeds on every plan; modular embedding with a React SDK; full app embedding with SSO on Pro and Enterprise.
- **Not ideal for:** design-heavy dashboards, or large rollouts that need governance without paying for Pro.


## Zoho Analytics


**Best for:** small and midsize businesses that want a shelf-based builder, business-app imports, and an AI agent at a low published price.


You drag columns into the X-axis, Y-axis, Color, Text, and Tooltip shelves, and Zia Suggestions lists the chart types that fit ([creating charts](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/chart/create-new-chart.html) ). Ask Zia is now agentic: it suggests formulas, writes SQL, builds pipelines, and creates reports and dashboards, while Zia Insights writes descriptive, predictive, diagnostic, and prescriptive narratives ([Zia](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/zia/) ). The pricing page puts the Ask Zia agent on Premium and Enterprise, Ask Zia chat on Standard and up, and instant Zia insights on Premium and up ([pricing](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/pricing.html) ).


**Fact card: Zoho Analytics**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** Basic $24 (2 users), Standard $48 (5), Premium $115 (15), Enterprise $455 (50) per month billed annually; $30, $60, $145, and $575 monthly. Extra users $8 a month.
- **Free tier or trial:** free plan with 2 users and 10,000 rows; 15-day trial.
- **Deployment:** cloud, or Zoho Analytics On-Premise.
- **Databases and query model:** Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL by import with scheduled syncs, or Live Connect on Premium and Enterprise; a Live Connect workspace can’t mix in other sources ([Snowflake](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/help/cloud-database/snowflake.html) ).
- **Access control:** row filters on shared views, such as matching a column to` ${System.login.email}` ; SAML through Zoho Directory; SCIM not documented.
- **AI features:** Zia Suggestions, Ask Zia chat and agent, Zia Insights, and AI Studio for MCP clients.
- **Embedding:** iframes; private permalinks on Premium and Enterprise; SDKs for embedded customers.
- **Not ideal for:** warehouse-live dashboards on a low plan.


## Sigma


**Best for:** teams on Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery whose analysts and finance users think in spreadsheets.


Sigma is the main answer for mixed spreadsheet and SQL users. Workbooks have tables and pivots like a spreadsheet and dashboard layouts like a BI tool, and you drag elements on a snap grid ([workbooks](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/workbooks-overview) ); every action compiles to SQL in your warehouse. Sigma Assistant answers in natural language and builds dashboards in the workbook, and the formula assistant writes and explains formulas ([AI features](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/configure-ai-features-for-your-organization) ). An admin must connect an AI provider first. Sigma agent messages are free until November 1, 2026, then cost 0.1 credit each ([billable usage](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/about-billable-usage-events) ).


**Fact card: Sigma**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** quote only; View, Act, Analyze, and Build license tiers plus credits for input tables, API calls, exports, and agent messages.
- **Free tier or trial:** 7-day trial, no credit card ([trial](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/start-your-sigma-trial) ).
- **Deployment:** SaaS on AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
- **Databases and query model:** Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, and others; live queries with optional materialization.
- **Access control:** RLS by user attribute, team, or email, or warehouse RLS over OAuth ([RLS](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/row-level-security) ); SAML; SCIM requires SAML.
- **AI features:** Sigma Assistant, Sigma agents, formula assistant, and Snowflake Cortex or Databricks Genie agents.
- **Embedding:** public and JWT-signed embeds and a React SDK; embedded Sigma Assistant is deprecated.
- **Not ideal for:** teams without a cloud warehouse, or buyers who need a published price.


## Qlik Cloud Analytics


**Best for:** midsize and larger organizations that want associative exploration and capacity pricing with no per-user charge.


You drag a chart from the assets panel onto a sheet, then drag fields onto it as dimensions or measures ([creating sheets](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Sheets/sheets-creating.htm) ); each selection then highlights related values across every chart. Insight Advisor turns a question into visualizations from the Starter plan up ([Insight Advisor](https://help.qlik.com/en-us/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Insights/insight-advisor-create-visualizations.htm) ). Where a tenant turns on agentic Qlik Answers, it replaces Insight Advisor and generates sheets and charts from conversation, after you opt in to cross-region inference ([Qlik Answers](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense%5FHub/QlikAnswers/Qlik-Answers.htm) ). Qlik’s docs put Answers on Standard and up, but the pricing page lists Answers agents on Starter, so confirm before buying Starter for it.


**Fact card: Qlik Cloud Analytics**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** billed annually. Starter $300/mo for 10 users and 10 GB; Standard $825/mo for 25 GB with no charge for extra users; Premium $2,750/mo for 50 GB; Enterprise custom ([pricing](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) ).
- **Free tier or trial:** 30-day Premium trial, no credit card.
- **Deployment:** Qlik Cloud, or client-managed Qlik Sense Enterprise on Windows.
- **Databases and query model:** Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL; in-memory apps, or Direct Query apps limited to one database each.
- **Access control:** section access on rows, columns, or both ([section access](https://help.qlik.com/en-us/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Scripting/Security/manage-security-with-section-access.htm) ); SAML and SCIM, plan not documented.
- **AI features:** Insight Advisor, Qlik Answers, Qlik Predict (Premium and Enterprise), and an MCP server on all plans.
- **Embedding:** qlik-embed web components and iframes; anonymous access on Premium.
- **Not ideal for:** small teams that want simple per-user pricing, or anyone avoiding Qlik’s load scripts.


## Domo


**Best for:** organizations that want unlimited users on consumption pricing, with connectors, ETL, and dashboards in one platform.


Domo’s Analyzer turns a dataset into a card as you drag columns into the chart’s fields ([Analyzer](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/Analyzer-Overview) ). AI Chat “lets you talk with your data from inside Domo,” and the Beast Mode AI Assistant writes calculated fields from the dataset schema ([AI services](https://www.domo.com/docs/portal/data-science/ai-services) ). AI Chat costs 0.2 credits per request, and customer-provided models consume none ([consumption terms](https://www.domo.com/consumption-terms) ). Progress Software completed its $400 million acquisition of Domo’s platform business on September 22, 2026 ([Progress announcement](https://investors.progress.com/news-releases/news-release-details/progress-software-completes-acquisition-domos-ai-and-data) ).


**Fact card: Domo**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** credit-based consumption, unlimited users, custom quotes ([pricing](https://www.domo.com/pricing) ).
- **Free tier or trial:** 30-day trial, no credit card.
- **Deployment:** cloud.
- **Databases and query model:** imports by default, including PostgreSQL; live queries on Snowflake and BigQuery (pushdown in beta) through Cloud Integrations, also called Cloud Amplifier ([Cloud Integrations](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/4412849158167) ).
- **Access control:** PDP row policies by user or group ([PDP](https://www.domo.com/docs/portal/Governance/pdp) ); SAML or OIDC SSO and SCIM ([SSO](https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/000005827) ).
- **AI features:** AI Chat, Beast Mode AI Assistant, an SQL editor assistant, and Agent Catalyst.
- **Embedding:** Domo Everywhere; public embeds don’t support PDP.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that need a predictable bill before they know usage, or buyers wary of a platform changing owners.


## Basedash


**Best for:** teams that would rather describe a dashboard than drag one, on Postgres, Snowflake, BigQuery, or synced SaaS data.


Basedash is here as the alternative to field-level drag-and-drop. You create a chart by asking in chat, describing it on a dashboard (“daily signups over the last 30 days, broken down by plan”), or writing SQL; the AI writes the query and picks the chart type ([charts docs](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/charts) ). After that, the point-and-click parts are familiar: settings for the X-axis, value, and breakdown columns, and a layout where you drag and resize charts and add tabs and text ([dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/features/dashboards) ). Every chart keeps its SQL and a history that shows whether each change came from a person or the AI. There is no shelf to drag a field onto, so Tableau-trained analysts will find it different rather than easier.


**Fact card: Basedash**


- **Pricing (as of October 2026):** flat fee plus AI usage. Startup $1,000/mo plus AI usage for up to 25 users, with $1,000/mo in AI credits; Enterprise custom ([pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ).
- **Free tier or trial:** 14-day trial, no credit card.
- **Deployment:** cloud; self-hosting on Enterprise ([self-hosting](https://www.basedash.com/features/self-hosting) ).
- **Databases and query model:** live queries against Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, ClickHouse, and others, plus 750+ SaaS sources synced into Basedash Warehouse ([data sources](https://www.basedash.com/docs/data-sources/introduction) ); dashboards refresh every 15 minutes by default.
- **Access control:** per-source access by group and AI data visibility controls on every plan; RLS through Postgres and Supabase policies only ([RLS docs](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/row-level-security) ); SAML or OIDC SSO and SCIM on Enterprise ([SSO docs](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/sso) ).
- **AI features:** an[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) that answers in chat with charts, prompt-built dashboards with filters, scheduled insights that explain what moved, and an[MCP server](https://www.basedash.com/features/mcp-server) .
- **Embedding:** Enterprise, with a React SDK or iframes ([embedding](https://www.basedash.com/features/embedding) ).
- **Not ideal for:** teams that want a visual builder as the main workflow, RLS on Snowflake or BigQuery, or a free tier.


## Which drag-and-drop BI tool should you choose?


**You want the best drag-and-drop interface.** Tableau, then Power BI, both with AI on the same canvas. Zoho Analytics has a similar shelf builder for much less.


**You want drag-and-drop plus AI insights on a small budget.** Metabase with your own API key costs only the provider’s tokens, and Zoho Analytics Premium ($115 a month billed annually for 15 users) includes the Ask Zia agent and Zia Insights. Data Studio is free, but its AI chat covers only BigQuery data agents.


**You need BigQuery and an LLM that explains trends in plain English.** Data Studio’s Conversational Analytics is the free native option. Power BI, Tableau, Zoho Analytics, Qlik, and Sigma all connect to BigQuery, and their assistants work on that data at the plan levels above. Our[BigQuery dashboarding comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-dashboarding-tools-for-bigquery-2026) goes deeper.


**You want usage-based or capacity pricing.** Domo charges credits with unlimited users, Qlik Standard and Premium price on data capacity, and Basedash charges a flat fee plus AI usage. Our guide to[BI tools with usage-based pricing](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-with-usage-based-pricing-2026) compares the models.


**Your team mixes spreadsheet and SQL users.** Sigma’s workbooks suit that mix best, and Metabase lets the same people switch between the query builder and SQL. If analysts want the model in Git, see our[BI-as-code guide](https://www.basedash.com/blog/bi-as-code-how-to-version-control-dashboards-metrics-and-semantic-models) .


**Nobody wants to build charts at all.** A prompt-first tool such as Basedash, or the AI side of Power BI or Tableau if you already pay for it, skips the builder. Our[BI tools for non-technical teams](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-for-non-technical-teams-in-2026) comparison covers that case.


**You need RLS, SAML, and SCIM on one plan.** Metabase Pro covers all three from $575 a month. Tableau, Sigma, Qlik, and Domo document all three; Basedash has SSO and SCIM on Enterprise.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which BI tool has the best drag-and-drop interface?


Tableau has the most complete drag-and-drop builder: you drag fields onto the Rows, Columns, and Marks shelves, and Show Me suggests chart types that fit. Power BI is a close second, with a field-to-visual workflow that feels familiar to Excel users. Zoho Analytics copies the shelf model at a much lower price, Qlik adds associative selections across every chart, and Sigma uses a spreadsheet layout instead of shelves. Analysts tend to prefer Tableau; Excel users tend to prefer Power BI or Sigma.


### What is the best drag-and-drop dashboard software with AI insights?


As of October 2026, Power BI with Copilot and Tableau with Tableau Agent have the strongest AI inside a drag-and-drop builder, because both generate visuals or report pages you then edit by hand. Both cost extra: Fabric F2 or Premium P1 capacity for Copilot, Tableau Cloud+ or Tableau+ for Tableau Agent. Zoho Analytics Premium includes the Ask Zia agent and Zia Insights for $115 a month billed annually, and Metabase’s Metabot runs on any plan with your own API key.


### Can AI automatically create charts when I ask a question?


Yes, in most current BI tools. Metabase’s Metabot turns a question into an editable query-builder chart, Tableau Agent and Power BI Copilot build visuals and report pages, Qlik’s Insight Advisor and Qlik Answers generate charts and sheets, Zoho’s Ask Zia agent creates reports, and Basedash builds charts and whole dashboards from a prompt. Accuracy depends on clear table and column names and defined metrics, so check the generated query before you share the result.


### Which drag-and-drop BI tools have usage-based pricing?


Domo is the clearest example: credit-based consumption with unlimited users, where AI Chat costs 0.2 credits per request. Qlik Cloud Analytics Standard and Premium price on data capacity and don’t charge for additional users. Sigma meters input tables, exports, and agent messages in credits but sells licenses by quote. Basedash charges a flat $1,000 a month plus AI usage for up to 25 users. Tableau, Power BI, Metabase, and Zoho Analytics price per seat or per plan.


### Is Looker Studio still free, and is it the same as Data Studio?


Yes. Google renamed Looker Studio back to Data Studio in April 2026, and lookerstudio.google.com links redirect to datastudio.google.com. Creating and viewing reports is still free. The paid edition, Data Studio Pro, costs $9 per user per project per month as of October 2026 with a 30-day trial, and adds Gemini features such as calculated fields written in plain English. There is no Google-built Snowflake connector; Snowflake data comes through partner connectors.


### Should I pick a code-first BI tool or a drag-and-drop tool for a mixed team?


Pick by who maintains the definitions. If analysts own metrics and want changes reviewed in pull requests, a code-first tool such as Looker or Lightdash keeps the model in Git while business users explore on top. If most builders live in spreadsheets or Excel, Sigma or Power BI fits better, with Metabase as a cheaper middle ground because the same chart can come from its query builder or from SQL. Many teams pair a modeled warehouse with a drag-and-drop or AI front end.
